title: feat(M0118-0001): read-only-anomaly-3 isolation spec passes — SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE safe-snapshot deferral
window:
The O'Neil read-only transaction anomaly: s3 is declared SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY
DEFERRABLE. PostgreSQL avoids the anomaly without aborting anyone by deferring
s3's snapshot (GetSafeSnapshot) until a safe snapshot is available — s3r blocks
(<waiting ...>) while the concurrent read-write s2 is active, then completes once
[...]
Two blockers fixed:

1. DEFERRABLE was never parsed: it lexes as the unreserved keyword token
   KwDeferrable, but parseBeginModes matched it with acceptIdentKeyword (TokenIdent
   only), so BEGIN ... READ ONLY DEFERRABLE failed with "syntax error ... got
   deferrable". Now matched with acceptKeyword(KwDeferrable); recorded in the new
   BeginStmt.Deferrable / Transaction.Deferrable plan field.

2. No safe-snapshot deferral existed. SerializableXact gains ReadOnly/Deferrable
   flags (set after Begin by Manager.MarkSerializableModes, wired in BOTH BEGIN
   paths — executor execBegin and server/dispatch.go auto-commit promotion).
   Manager.SnapshotFor calls Manager.waitForSafeSnapshot before capturing a
   SERIALIZABLE xact's first snapshot: a ReadOnly+Deferrable xact enrolls every
   concurrent declared-read-write SERIALIZABLE xact active at that instant and
   blocks on a sync.Cond (ssiCond, bound to ssiMu) until each has FinishedAt
   stamped (commit or abort); releaseSerializableLocked broadcasts on finish. A
   snapshot taken after all writers drain is always RO_SAFE, so the reader is
   never aborted. No-op for every non-deferrable serializable workload.

Deliberate divergence (design §17): no RO_UNSAFE early-abort/retry refinement —
the sole DEFERRABLE spec resolves to a safe snapshot; the deferral is a pure
false-positive eliminator (worst un-modelled case waits longer, never wrong).

  goroutine doesn't respond promptly to context cancellation.

and returns the XID to probeArbiterWaiting, which then blocks on

matches the insert-conflict-do-update-4.spec expected behavior where s1
